name: Venom Reach

stars.name: Hemlock
stars.notes: Intense UV emitter with irregular mass ejection events. Luminosity roughly 4,500 times solar.

planets.name: Strychnos
planets.notes: Tidally locked. The dayside is a permanent lava ocean; the nightside is fractured basalt venting sulfur dioxide in towering plumes.

planets.name: Banebreath
planets.notes: Dense toxic atmosphere of hydrogen cyanide and carbon monoxide. Atmospheric pressure at the surface is 47 atm. The name is literal.

planets.name: Nightshade
planets.notes: Frozen surface concealing a subsurface ocean of ammonia-laced brine. Periodic cryovolcanic eruptions spray toxic slush hundreds of kilometers high.

planets.name: Oleander
planets.notes: Atmosphere rich in hydrogen sulfide and phosphine. Visible bands of sickly yellow-green give the planet a diseased appearance.

anomalies.name: The Bile Nebula
anomalies.location: Pervading inner system between orbits 1 and 3
anomalies.notes: Remnant of a proto-planetary accretion event rich in cyanide compounds and sulfur particulates. Corrodes exposed metal components. Danger level: high.

anomalies.name: Hemlock's Spite
anomalies.location: Variable; erupts from Hemlock on 40-60 day cycles
anomalies.notes: Massive coronal ejections blanket the inner system in charged particle storms. Unshielded electronics fail within minutes. Danger level: extreme.

anomalies.name: The Acid Veil
anomalies.location: Surrounding Banebreath in a 0.3 AU radius
anomalies.notes: Atmospheric escape from Banebreath has created a diffuse cloud of corrosive compounds in local space. Eats through standard hull sealants. Danger level: high.

asteroid_belts.name: The Toxin Ring
asteroid_belts.composition: sulfide-rich metallic fragments and carbonaceous material
asteroid_belts.notes: Asteroids coated in sulfur compounds that outgas when disturbed, creating local hazard clouds around mining operations.

stations.name: Probe Sentinel VR-7
stations.notes: Automated monitoring probe studying Hemlock's ejection cycles. Transmits data via tightbeam relay. Third unit deployed; predecessors destroyed by coronal events.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. The Blight Expanse Survey Authority maintains a navigational hazard beacon at the system's edge.

history: First surveyed in 2501 by the long-range probe 'Haruspex,' which returned data on Banebreath's atmosphere composition. The probe's outer hull showed severe corrosion upon recovery.

A corporate mining expedition in 2548 attempted to extract sulfide-rich ores from the Toxin Ring. The crew of the freighter 'Dividend' suffered catastrophic hull seal failure from chemical corrosion and were lost with all hands.
Venom Reach was formally designated a Class IV Chemical Hazard Zone in 2553. Approach requires sealed environmental suits and corrosion-resistant hull coatings rated for cyanide exposure.
description: Venom Reach is a system that seems purpose-built to poison anything that enters it. Hemlock, a young B2V star, bathes its four worlds in intense ultraviolet radiation, but the true danger lies in the chemistry. Every body in this system is saturated with toxic compounds: hydrogen cyanide, hydrogen sulfide, phosphine, carbon monoxide, and sulfur dioxide in concentrations that corrode metal, destroy organic material, and overwhelm standard life-support filtration.

The hazards are layered and overlapping. The Bile Nebula suffuses the inner system with corrosive particulates. Hemlock's Spite delivers periodic electromagnetic storms that fry unshielded electronics. The Acid Veil around Banebreath dissolves hull sealants. Even the asteroid belt outgasses poison when disturbed. The cumulative effect means that any ship spending more than a few days in-system without specialized chemical-resistant modifications will begin to experience critical seal failures.

Despite the dangers, Venom Reach holds minor scientific interest. Banebreath's extreme toxic atmosphere is a natural laboratory for prebiotic chemistry studies, and Nightshade's ammonia ocean may harbor exotic chemical processes. The automated probe VR-7, the third of its kind, continues to transmit data from the system's outer reaches. No crewed mission has been authorized since the loss of the Dividend, and the few ships that pass through do so at maximum speed with sealed external systems.
